introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (English Language 1, June 2023, Ordinary/Intermediate Level). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. The paper has four sections: A listening comprehension (questions 1-10), B reading comprehension (questions 11-25), C grammar (questions 26-40) and D vocabulary (questions 41-50).
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Questions 20 et 40 : la clé n'est pas établie avec certitude, donc ingérées comme questions OUVERTES (auto-évaluation). Q20 ("travelling" dans "travelling documents") : A gerund contre D adjective, les deux analyses sont défendables. Q40 (ponctuation) : aucune des quatre versions imprimées n'est entièrement correcte, D (point puis "However" sans virgule) est la plus proche mais B (comma splice) est peut-être la clé du Board.
Question 5 : clé C (contagious) ; le passage ne dit pas « contagious » mais décrit la transmission de personne à personne. A (common) est l'option concurrente.
Question 11 : clé B (prostitution) ; D (trafficking of women) est l'option concurrente, le texte emploie « trade » juste après « trafficking ».
Question 19 : clé B (stolen) ; le passage ne donne pas la raison, B est la plus réaliste. Concurrente : D (hidden).
Question 21 : clé B (most dignifying) d'après « the most honourable thing to do » ; le libellé de la question reste approximatif.
Question 41 : clé B (relieved of his duties, collocation avec « of »). Concurrente : D (dismissed), qui demanderait « from ».
Le sujet imprime « which in correctly punctuated » à la question 40 : coquille corrigée en « which is correctly punctuated ».

Les mots soulignés des questions 47 à 50 sont rendus en gras, faute de souligné fiable en Markdown. Les numéros de ligne du passage de lecture sont repris entre crochets, à la fin de la ligne imprimée.

Le texte de l'écoute (Section A) vient des pages d'instructions du professeur, recopié sans les barres obliques de pause. Les titres « Section One/Two/Three » du livret correspondent aux questions 1-4, 5-7 et 8-10.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Listening passage (read aloud once by the examiner in the real exam - read it once, then answer)**

**Section 1**

Dear friends, today I am going to talk to you about disease prevention and staying healthy. "Hand washing is the single most important thing that you can do to help prevent the spread of infection and to stay healthy and well." As many as 80 percent of infections are said to be passed on by unclean hands, so wash them throughout the day. Do so especially before eating, preparing food, dressing, touching a wound, and after touching an animal, using the toilet or changing a baby's diaper.

Washing with soap and water is more effective than using alcohol based hand sanitizers. Children stay healthier when parents train them to wash and keep their hands away from their mouths and eyes. Bathing every day and keeping your clothes and bed linen fresh and clean also contribute to better health.

**Section 2**

Avoid close physical contact or the sharing of eating utensils with anyone who has a cold or flu. Their saliva and nasal secretions can pass the illness onto you. Blood borne diseases as hepatitis B and C and HIV/AIDS are transmitted primarily through sexual contact, intravenous drug use and blood transfusion. Although vaccination can help to prevent some infections, a wise person must still take necessary precautions when someone has an infectious disease. Do not sleep or sit outdoors unprotected when mosquitoes or other disease-carrying insects are active.

**Section 3**

Make whatever extra effort is needed to keep your home tidy and clean inside and outside. Eliminate any place where water can collect and mosquitoes can breed. Litter, filth, uncovered foods and garbage attract insects and vermin, all of which can bring in microbes and cause diseases. If there is no toilet, build a simple latrine rather than just relieving yourself in a field. Cover the latrine to keep out flies, which transmit eye infection and other diseases. So my dear friends, if we respect all these rules, we will stay healthy.

**Section A - Listening comprehension (5 marks).** Using only the material read to you from the listening comprehension passage, answer each of the following questions as directed. Choose the best answer from the alternatives (A, B, C and D) for each of the questions below.

**Section One**

1. \_\_\_\_\_\_ is the main thing one can do to prevent the spread of infection.
questions.corrige_markdown: The speaker quotes the sentence "Hand washing is the single most important thing that you can do to help prevent the spread of infection". Health care, body washing and disease control are not given as the main measure. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section One

2. In the passage we are advised to wash our hands \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The speaker says "wash them throughout the day" and lists many occasions (before eating, after the toilet, and so on), so hands should be washed as often as needed. No fixed number of times and no single occasion is given. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section One

3. The expression "Do so" read to you from the passage refers to \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Do so" repeats the verb phrase of the previous sentence, "wash them" (your hands): "Do so especially before eating, preparing food...". Dressing, touching a wound and preparing food are occasions on which to wash, not what "do so" means. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section One

4. According to the passage, it is best to wash hands using \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says "Washing with soap and water is more effective than using alcohol based hand sanitizers". The best method is therefore water and soap. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

5. Cold and flu are considered as \_\_\_\_\_\_ diseases.
questions.corrige_markdown: Section 2 warns against close contact and shared utensils with someone who has a cold or flu, because their saliva and nasal secretions "can pass the illness onto you". Diseases that pass from person to person are contagious. "Common" is true in life but is not what the passage says, and no water or air route is mentioned. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

6. You have heard the word "physical" read to you from the passage. Which word from the list below has the same stress pattern as in "physical"?
questions.corrige_markdown: "Physical" is stressed on the first syllable: PHYsical. Stress of the options: preVENtive (second syllable), PRINcipal (first), preTENtious (second), proTECted (second). Only "principal" matches. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

7. Infectious diseases can be prevented by \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Section 2 states "vaccination can help to prevent some infections". Daily bathing is mentioned in Section 1 only as a contribution to better health, and sitting outdoors unprotected is warned against. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

8. Litter, filth, uncovered food and garbage attract \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says "Litter, filth, uncovered foods and garbage attract insects and vermin, all of which can bring in microbes". Microbes and infections are brought in by the insects and vermin; they are not what is attracted. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

9. Flies can transmit infections of the \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says flies "transmit eye infection and other diseases". **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

10. This talk could have been delivered by a \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The whole talk gives advice on disease prevention and hygiene to the public ("Dear friends..."), which is the work of a health worker. A veterinary doctor deals with animals, and a counsellor or teacher would not normally give this kind of health talk. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section B - Reading comprehension (7½ marks).** Read the passage below carefully and answer the questions which follow.

**Passage for questions 11 to 25** (the numbers in square brackets are the line numbers printed in the paper)

Female prostitution has become a common phenomenon around the world. There is a lot of trafficking of women going on. Every year, many young women are recruited for **this trade**. These women are given false hopes that they would have good jobs, marriages, and opportunities of various kinds that do not exist. They are given free visas and made to understand that they are the ones to solve the problem of poverty in their families. Accepting all these as true, these women and their parents enter into agreements as a way of improving on their [5] family situations.

When they arrive at the port of entry, these women are forced into prostitution. Most often, they have no knowledge of the local language. They are **totally at the mercy of the perpetrators** who threaten them and if they do not co-operate, they are abused and sometimes killed. Some of these women are sold **from one "madam"** to another and finally they are exposed to different men, with different characters and behaviour, who [10] use them as sex objects. These traffickers do not leave them till they have worked for them and paid all they spent in getting them abroad.

It is sad that a good number of Africans are still blind to this new system of slavery. How can a parent expect his/her daughter who is not educated and has no qualification of any sort to get a decent job abroad? Even when she is educated, how can a stranger offer one a good job just like that? Let this passage educate Africans who want to live out of their countries. When they win the so called lottery, it will only permit them to go there [15] but they must look for what to do when they get there.

America or Europe is not a paradise as many Africans mistakenly think. They are like any other place in the world where people have to struggle to survive. When people entertain the idea of going overseas, they must make sure that their travelling is legal and that they have a sense of purpose. They must protect the good image of their own country by not trying to go through the back door because in the end, they will destroy their image [20] and that of their country. One needs genuine **travelling documents** like a passport and the necessary visa to enter the country. One needs a work and residence permit to have a good job and to live a peaceful life in the country of destination. It is important to keep in mind that there is also a high level of unemployment abroad and it is not easy to get a good job. Actually, women would never get all the money they make from prostitution, for what they get is far less than what they put in. The mental torture and the dangers involved in the prostitution [25] business are unbearable and not worth the sacrifice. It is important to know that when one cannot get the job one wants, one will be forced to accept any type of job just to survive.

If people must go abroad, they must make sure they have valid travelling documents and they know the people who are assisting them to travel very well. Travellers should endeavour to find out from the embassy of the country of their destination if the type of job opportunity they are being offered exists; and the authenticity of [30] the company inviting them. They should contact bodies in their country that can assist them with useful information. Migrants should not travel without the knowledge of their family. It is important for family to know departure dates, name and address of travelling companions and even have their photographs. In this way a lawyer can be contacted in case their relative gets into trouble. The lawyer may be able to assist his clients and obtain free services. Passports should never be handed to anybody. [35]

The worst situation is that there are many women and men who are ashamed to come back home when they discover that they have been deceived because they feel they have failed their families. It is never too late to realize one's mistake and come home. In fact, it is the most honourable thing to do. There is no other place like home. **Time has come for Africans to look for their "salvation" among themselves and in their own home lands.** Most of the jobs Africans agree to do abroad are jobs they would not ordinarily do back in their home [40] country. Africa is blessed with rich human and material resources. These only need to be exploited and the dividends used for the good of all.

I believe strongly that Africans can start now to build their countries with the gifts they have. Let us stop running away from our countries. We have many gifts, and all we need is to support one another, appreciate our gifts and those of others; join all forces to build solid nations where every citizen will feel at [45] home. East or West home is best.

**Questions 11 to 25**

11. "This trade" (line 2) refers to \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage opens with "Female prostitution" and says young women are recruited for "this trade"; the next paragraph says they are "forced into prostitution" and later refers to "the prostitution business". The trade they are recruited for is prostitution. Trafficking is the means by which they are moved, not the trade itself. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 12. According to the passage, the mistake made by the young women is that they \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: They are "given false hopes" of jobs and marriages that "do not exist" and they accept "all these as true". Their mistake is failing to see that the promises are false. Hoping for jobs is not itself the mistake. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: are too excited about going abroad
hope to have jobs and good opportunities
fail to realize the falsehood in the promises made to them
fail to see how expensive their venture is

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 13. The expression "totally at the mercy of the perpetrators" (line 8) suggests that the women \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: To be "at the mercy of" someone means to be completely in that person's power, unable to protect oneself. Option C says this. Option D is a literal reading of the word "mercy" and is a trap; the phrase describes helplessness, not how they are treated. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

choix.texte: cannot find their way back home
depend on their masters for livelihood
are helpless in the hands of their masters

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 14. Some of the women are abused or killed because they \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says the perpetrators threaten them "and if they do not co-operate, they are abused and sometimes killed". Not co-operating means being unwilling to give in. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: are not willing to give in
want to expose the deeds of traffickers

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 15. In the expression "from one madam" (lines 9 and 10) the word "madam" refers to \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The women are "sold from one madam to another" and then exposed to men who use them as sex objects. A madam here is a woman who runs and controls prostitutes. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

choix.texte: a woman in charge of prostitutes

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 16. According to the passage, it is rather \_\_\_\_\_\_ that jobs Africans readily do overseas are jobs they would not do back in their own countries.
questions.corrige_markdown: The writer points out a contradiction: Africans accept abroad the jobs they refuse at home. A situation that is the opposite of what one would expect is ironical. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 17. No amount of money got from prostitution can make up for the \_\_\_\_\_\_ involved.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 24 to 26 say "The mental torture and the dangers involved in the prostitution business are unbearable and not worth the sacrifice". Option C copies this idea. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 18. It is necessary for a person who is to travel abroad for a given job to enquire from the embassy of the country of his/her destination whether the job offered him/her exists and what the inviting company does because this will \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The embassy check tests "the authenticity of the company" and whether the job exists, which protects the traveller from being deceived (see also the earlier warning about false hopes). Payment and ease of travel are not the purpose given. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: enable the person to know if he/she is being deceived/tricked
help the person know if the payment is attractive or not
enable him/her to arrive his/her destination with ease

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 19. It is not good for a person to hand over his/her passport to anybody because it could be \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage only says "Passports should never be handed to anybody". Of the four options, the realistic danger of giving a valuable document to a stranger is that it could be stolen (and misused), so B is the best answer. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 20. In the phrase "travelling documents" (line 21) "travelling" is used as a/an \_\_\_\_\_\_.

*Options as printed:* A) gerund   B) adverb   C) verb   D) adjective
questions.corrige_markdown:
"Travelling documents" means "documents for travelling". Strictly, "travelling" is a gerund used as a modifier of the noun, like "walking stick" or "swimming pool" (a stick for walking, a pool for swimming). Many school grammars, however, call such a word an adjective because it describes the noun "documents". It is not an adverb (it does not modify a verb) and it is not a finite verb here.

Because both the gerund and the adjective analyses are defended and the Board's key is not known, this question is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**Answer: gerund (A), strictly; adjective (D) is also commonly accepted.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 21. According to the writer, failing to realize one's dreams abroad and coming back home is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 35 to 38: those who find they were deceived should "come home. In fact, it is the most honourable thing to do." "Honourable" is close in meaning to "dignifying". **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

choix.texte: the most dignifying thing to do

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 22. The expression "Time has come for Africans to work for their salvation among themselves and their home lands." (lines 39-40) implies that Africans \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence urges Africans to find their "salvation" (their way out) at home, and the next lines explain how: Africa's rich resources "only need to be exploited and the dividends used for the good of all". So the implication is self-development through their own resources. Option D is stated in the passage but is not what this sentence implies. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: have had enough of stress from abroad
can develop themselves by making good use of their resources
are a blessing in disguise to Europe
are blessed with lots of natural resources

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 23. The unexploited blessings of Africa are \_\_\_\_\_\_ resources.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 40 to 42: "Africa is blessed with rich human and material resources. These only need to be exploited...". The resources named are human and material. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 24. Africans will be self-sufficient and independent the moment they \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The closing paragraph says "Africans can start now to build their countries with the gifts they have". That is the condition for self-sufficiency. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: start developing their countries with the gifts they have
start monitoring the rate of exodus

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage for questions 11 to 25 above) 25. The message the author of this passage seems to be emphasizing is that \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage ends with "Let us stop running away from our countries... East or West home is best": Africans can succeed in their own countries. Options C and D describe the mistaken belief the writer criticizes, and B is only a supporting detail. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Africans can make it back home
there is high unemployment in Europe and Africa
Africans think they need Europe to make it in life
Africans see Europe as a paradise

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section C - Grammar (7½ marks).** Read the instructions for each question or set of questions carefully before answering. Choose the best answer that completes each sentence.

26. If he had attended the party, he \_\_\_\_\_\_ me.
questions.corrige_markdown: This is the third conditional ("if" + past perfect), so the main clause takes "would have" + past participle: "would have seen". **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 27. Whenever you buy an article, insist \_\_\_\_\_\_ being given a receipt.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb "insist" is followed by the preposition "on": insist on being given. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 28. The most recent shootout resulted \_\_\_\_\_\_ the death of many.
questions.corrige_markdown: The fixed phrase is "result in" (cause something): resulted in the death of many. "Result from" would name the cause instead. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 29. The mathematics teacher taught citizenship because there wasn't \_\_\_\_\_\_ to teach it.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Wasn't" is already negative, so a negative word such as "nobody" would make a double negative. After a negative verb we use "anybody": there wasn't anybody else. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 30. Amanda is the captain of the \_\_\_\_\_\_ football team.
questions.corrige_markdown: A team of several girls needs the plural possessive: the girls' football team (plural noun ending in s, then an apostrophe). "Girl's" would mean one girl's team. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - spelling and punctuation

questions.enonce_markdown: 31. You won't tell anybody, \_\_\_\_\_\_?
questions.corrige_markdown: A question tag reverses the polarity of the statement. The statement is negative (won't), so the tag is positive and repeats the auxiliary: "will you". **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 32. If he \_\_\_\_\_\_ the truth, I would have forgiven him.
questions.corrige_markdown: The main clause "would have forgiven" shows the third conditional, so the "if" clause needs the past perfect: "had told". **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 33. Not \_\_\_\_\_\_ did she refuse to speak to me, but she also vowed never to see me again.
questions.corrige_markdown: The correlative pair is "not only ... but also". With "Not only" at the start of the sentence, the auxiliary comes before the subject ("did she refuse"). "Simply", "just" and "merely" do not pair with "but also". **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 34. Lukong is not happy with his present job \_\_\_\_\_\_ the salary is very low.
questions.corrige_markdown: The second clause gives the reason for his unhappiness, so a conjunction of reason is needed: "as" (because). "Although" and "even if" express contrast and make no sense here, and "in spite" must be followed by "of". **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 35. Leaders who don't listen \_\_\_\_\_\_ believe they have the answers.
questions.corrige_markdown: An adverb of frequency fits before the verb: "usually believe". "Likely" would need "are likely to believe", "badly" does not fit the meaning and "rightly" would contradict the point. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 36. The farmers look forward to \_\_\_\_\_\_ in agro-pastoral shows.
questions.corrige_markdown: In "look forward to" the word "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by the -ing form: "participating". "Participation" is a noun and would need a different structure (participation in...), and the bare infinitive or "have participation" are not possible after "to" here. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - gerunds and infinitives

questions.enonce_markdown: 37. The wind is \_\_\_\_\_\_ to blow the roof off.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Adjective + enough + to-infinitive" shows that the quality is sufficient for the result: strong enough to blow the roof off. "Too strong to" would mean the wind is so strong that it cannot do it, and "quite/very strong" cannot be followed by "to blow" in this sense. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - too and enough

questions.enonce_markdown: 38. The woman whom John \_\_\_\_\_\_ comes from Nigeria.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Whom" already stands for the woman, so a pronoun "her" would repeat it (options A and D are wrong). The correct phrase is "be engaged to" (promised in marriage), with the preposition left at the end: whom John is engaged to. "Has engaged her" means "hired her". **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 39. The mad lady was wearing a pair of \_\_\_\_\_\_ slippers.
questions.corrige_markdown: Adjectives follow the order opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material: size (small), then colour (red), then material (plastic). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
40. The sentence which is correctly punctuated is: \_\_\_\_\_\_.

*Options as printed:*

A) Alice has a busy schedule this week, however; she promises to be at the party.

B) Alice has a busy schedule this week, however, she promises to be at the party.

C) Alice has a busy schedule this week however; she promises to be at the party!

D) Alice has a busy schedule this week. However she promises to be at the party.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The standard punctuation is "Alice has a busy schedule this week; however, she promises to be at the party." (or a full stop, then "However," with a comma). None of the four printed versions is fully correct: A puts the semicolon after "however" instead of before it, and C has no comma, a misplaced semicolon and an exclamation mark. B joins two complete sentences with only a comma (a comma splice). D correctly splits the two sentences with a full stop and only omits the optional comma after "However", so it is the closest to correct. Because B is also a plausible intended key, this question is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**Answer: D is the closest to correct; B is the alternative the Board may have intended.**
themes: O Level English - spelling and punctuation

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section D - Vocabulary (5 marks).** Read the instructions for each question or set of questions carefully before answering.

**For numbers 41-46, choose the answer that best completes each sentence.**

41. After recording several absences from school, the class prefect was \_\_\_\_\_\_ of his duties.
questions.corrige_markdown: The fixed collocation is "relieved of his duties" (released from them). "Removed", "discharged" and "dismissed" take "from", not "of". **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 42. Many people are not well \_\_\_\_\_\_ in taking minutes.
questions.corrige_markdown: The idiom is "well versed in" (skilled and knowledgeable about). "Acquainted" takes "with", "efficient" takes "at" and "experienced" does not follow "well" in this idiom. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 43. The \_\_\_\_\_\_ took control of the plane by force.
questions.corrige_markdown: A person who takes control of an aircraft by force is a hijacker. A pilot flies the plane legitimately, a vandal destroys property and a burglar breaks into buildings. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 44. The police not only arrested the leader of the gang but also the \_\_\_\_\_\_ who had helped him.
questions.corrige_markdown: People who help someone to commit a crime are accomplices. "Associates" is too general (it does not imply crime), attackers are not necessarily helpers and solicitors are lawyers. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 45. Peter's behaviour brought \_\_\_\_\_\_ credit to his name.
questions.corrige_markdown: The prefix "dis-" gives the opposite meaning: discredit (loss of reputation). "Uncredit", "miscredit" and "incredit" do not exist. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 46. \_\_\_\_\_\_ was provided during our stay in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown: The correct spelling has a double c and a double m: ac-com-mo-da-tion. The other options drop one of the doubled letters (Accomodation: one m; Acommodation: one c; Acomodation: one c and one m). **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - spelling and punctuation

questions.enonce_markdown:
**For numbers 47 and 48, choose the answer that best explains the meaning of the underlined word (shown in bold here).**

47. I can't **force** them to attend the party.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Force" means to make someone do something against their will, which is "compel". "Persuade" and "convince" mean winning someone over by argument, the opposite approach, and "insist" does not take an object in this pattern. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms

questions.enonce_markdown: 48. At the age of twelve he showed **exceptional** talent as a footballer.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Exceptional" means unusually good, standing out from the rest, which is "outstanding". "Excellent" is close but does not carry the idea of being rare; "unequal" is unrelated and "renown" is a noun (the adjective would be "renowned"). **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms

questions.enonce_markdown:
**For numbers 49 and 50, choose the answer that gives the opposite of the underlined word (shown in bold here).**

49. The curtains were **transparent**.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Transparent" means that light passes through so that one can see through; its opposite is "opaque" (does not let light through). "Thick" and "dark" describe other qualities and "light" is not its opposite in this sense. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms

questions.enonce_markdown: 50. His speech was too **brief** for my liking.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Brief" means short in length, and its opposite is "lengthy" (long). "Expansive" means friendly and talkative, or wide in range, so it is not a direct opposite of short; "temporary" and "monotonous" are unrelated. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms
